morphology.summary: Not a sac but a single, continuous membrane network - a 'netlike labyrinth of branching tubules and flattened sacs' (Alberts) that all interconnect so the ER membrane forms one continuous sheet enclosing ONE continuous internal space, the ER lumen. It begins right at the nuclear envelope (the outer nuclear membrane IS rough ER membrane) and radiates out through the cytosol in two visually and functionally distinct regions that must both appear, connected, in one frame: ROUGH ER near the nucleus - stacked, flattened membrane sheets (cisternae) whose cytosolic face is densely studded with ribosomes, the site of co-translational protein folding and quality control - transitioning, without any wall or gap, into SMOOTH ER further out - a branching network of narrower TUBULES completely free of ribosomes, the site of lipid/steroid synthesis, detoxification and calcium storage. The ER membrane makes up more than half of the total membrane of an average animal cell, and the lumen alone can occupy over 10% of total cell volume - the largest membrane surface and one of the largest membrane-bound compartments in the cell.
morphology.kind: single continuous membrane-bound organelle of eukaryotic cells, physically continuous with the nuclear envelope (absent from bacteria/archaea)
morphology.size: Matches the atlas scale entry (10 um extent, ~300 pg): the whole network can span most of the cytosol from the nucleus to the cell periphery. Individual rough-ER cisternae are flattened sacs tens of nm to a few um across with a lumen typically ~20-50 nm wide (continuous with the nuclear envelope's perinuclear space); smooth-ER tubules are narrower, roughly 30-60 nm in diameter. Ribosomes studding the rough ER are ~25-30 nm particles, spaced closely and fairly regularly over the cytosolic membrane face.
morphology.shape: Rough ER: a stack of 2-8+ closely spaced, gently curved, flattened parallel sheets (cisternae), their outer (cytosolic) faces peppered with small dark ribosome dots at close, fairly regular spacing; the sheets run largely parallel to each other, sometimes whorled, and are all connected at their edges/ends rather than being separate discs. Smooth ER: a branching, anastomosing mesh of narrower tubules with no flat sheet character and no ribosomes, connected at Y- or X-shaped junctions, giving an open net rather than stacked sheets. Between the two, a transitional zone (transitional ER, tER) where cisternae narrow into a cluster of tubules and vesicle buds pinch off - this is the ER's dedicated export gateway, distinct from ordinary smooth ER, and it sits physically between the rough-ER stack and the Golgi apparatus, not scattered at random.
morphology.number_per_cell: One continuous ER network per cell (not multiple separate organelles) - all the sheets and tubules are literally one connected membrane and one connected lumen, however far apart they look in a 2D cutaway.
morphology.position_in_cell: Rough ER begins at, and its outer sheet is directly continuous with, the outer nuclear membrane; it typically radiates from the nuclear surface outward. Smooth ER lies further from the nucleus, often nearer the cell periphery/Golgi, and is generally much more sparse than rough ER in most cell types (a major exception: hepatocytes, with unusually extensive smooth ER for drug/xenobiotic detoxification; and muscle cells, where the smooth-ER-derived sarcoplasmic reticulum wraps the contractile apparatus to store/release calcium). A composition should never show a nucleus with no ER attached, and never show smooth ER floating disconnected from a rough-ER/nuclear-envelope source.
morphology.rough_er: Membrane sheets whose cytosolic face is coated with ribosomes (via the ribosome's large subunit docking at the translocon, Sec61); this is literally what makes it look 'rough' under EM. Ribosome-studded translation lets nascent secretory/membrane proteins be threaded directly into the ER lumen or membrane as they are made (co-translational translocation), where resident chaperones (e.g. BiP) and the ER's oxidising environment support folding and disulfide-bond formation, and a quality-control system retains misfolded proteins for refolding or ER-associated degradation. Ribosomes sit ONLY on the cytosolic face, never inside the lumen.
morphology.smooth_er: Tubular, ribosome-free membrane. In most cells a comparatively minor, partly-smooth/partly-rough component; in specialised cells (steroid-hormone-producing endocrine cells, and above all hepatocytes) it is greatly expanded. Its enzymes (including cytochrome P450 family members embedded in the membrane) synthesise lipids, phospholipids and steroid hormones, and metabolise/detoxify drugs and other lipophilic compounds by making them water-soluble enough to excrete - this is the biochemical basis of drug metabolism in the liver. It is also the main intracellular calcium store, released and re-sequestered through Ca2+ channels/pumps to trigger and end processes such as muscle contraction (as the sarcoplasmic reticulum, a specialised smooth ER wrapping each myofibril).
morphology.transitional_er: A specialised smooth-surfaced sub-region marking the boundary between rough ER and the Golgi, containing ER exit sites (ERES) where COPII-coated transport vesicles bud off, carrying correctly folded secretory and membrane proteins onward to the Golgi apparatus (cis-Golgi/ERGIC). Draw it as a cluster of small vesicle buds pinching from the smooth-tubule side of the network, oriented toward (but distinct from and smaller than) a Golgi stack if one is shown at all.
morphology.colour_note: Like any single organelle, the ER is essentially colourless/transparent in life and TEM is greyscale; all colour below is a teaching convention chosen for legibility and, per project convention, kept consistent with the grey-blue 'rough ER' tone already used for the Golgi-apparatus and nucleus plates in this same set.

structures.note: The single most important structure: several flattened, parallel membrane sheets, connected to one another and to the nuclear envelope, their cytosolic face densely studded with ribosomes. Must read as continuous sheets, never as separate sealed discs (that is the Golgi's look, not the ER's).

Many small, roughly equal-sized dark dots/particles evenly and closely spaced over the OUTER (cytosolic) face of the rough-ER sheets only. Never on the smooth-ER tubules. Never a handful - dense, regular studding is what makes rough ER 'rough'.

The narrow bright/pale space enclosed by the membrane, continuous all the way from the perinuclear space through every rough-ER cisterna into every smooth-ER tubule - one single connected interior, not separate pockets. Show it as a thin pale gap inside the membrane lines throughout both regions.

Narrower, rounded tubules branching and fusing into an open net, completely free of ribosomes, continuous with (not separate from) the rough-ER sheets - shown transitioning smoothly out of the stacked-cisternae region, never as an isolated patch with no connection to the rough ER.
A ribosome-free patch at the smooth-ER edge, closest to the Golgi if one is shown, where small round buds are actively pinching off the membrane.

structures.en: Transport vesicles budding toward the Golgi
structures.note: A few small round vesicles, freshly pinched off from the transitional-ER buds, positioned between the ER and (if shown) a small, clearly separate Golgi stack - carrying folded cargo onward, one-way, ER to Golgi.

structures.en: Continuity with the outer nuclear membrane
structures.note: The rough ER is not a free-floating organelle: at least one edge of the frame must show the nuclear envelope (two close parallel membrane lines) flowing directly, without any break or gap, into the nearest rough-ER cisterna, itself ribosome-studded like the ER.

Optional and, if included at all, must be small, off to one side, and visually subordinate - the Golgi is already its own subject plate in this atlas; do not let it compete with the ER for attention here.
Fills the frame around the network; may include a few free (non-ER) ribosomes, but the rough-to-smooth ER transition must dominate the composition.

do_not_draw: Do NOT show only rough ER or only smooth ER. The single most important thing this image must do is show BOTH in one frame, connected, with the contrast between them legible: stacked ribosome-studded sheets transitioning into a ribosome-free tubular network.

Do NOT put ribosomes on the smooth ER. Ribosomes belong ONLY on the cytosolic face of rough-ER cisternae (and, at the frame's edge, the outer nuclear membrane). Smooth-ER tubules must be completely bare.
Do NOT draw the ER as a closed bag, a single sac, or a handful of separate blobs. It is one continuous branching network of connected sheets and tubes enclosing one continuous lumen.

Do NOT draw the rough ER as stacked, isolated, unconnected discs with gaps between them and no continuity - that is a GOLGI STACK (a separate organelle, already its own subject plate in this atlas), the single most likely confusion. Golgi cisternae are discrete and separate; ER cisternae are continuous with each other and with the nuclear envelope.

Do NOT draw a nucleus with no ER attached, or ER floating with no visible connection to a nuclear envelope. The rough ER begins at, and its membrane is continuous with, the outer nuclear membrane - show that junction.
Do NOT draw cristae (the folded inner-membrane shelves of a mitochondrion) anywhere in this image - a different organelle entirely, do not let ER membrane whorls be mistaken for them.
Do NOT let a Golgi apparatus, if shown at all, dominate or compete with the ER for visual attention - keep it small and clearly downstream.
Do NOT add text, letters, numbers, scale bars, arrows-with-labels or watermarks baked into the image.
Do NOT anthropomorphise the ER in the SEM/textbook/3d/watercolor renders (no face, no eyes, no limbs) - that treatment is reserved separately for the coloring-book style only, per project convention.

colour_legend.rough_er_cisternae: #9AA7B5 (cool grey-blue sheet fill), same tone already used for 'rough ER' context in the Golgi-apparatus and nucleus plates of this set, so all three organelle images read as one consistent family
colour_legend.ribosomes_on_rer: #7A4438 (dark warm terracotta-brown dots), a compact blend of the ribosome organelle's own two-subunit palette (terracotta large subunit / blue small subunit), dense and evenly stippled on the rough-ER sheets only
colour_legend.er_lumen: #EAF1F5 (very pale blue-white, thin gap inside the membrane lines throughout both regions)
colour_legend.smooth_er_tubules: #B7C9C6 (lighter, slightly greener grey-blue than the rough-ER sheets - related but visibly distinct, like a chemistry-lab cousin of the workshop-floor rough ER), no ribosome dots
colour_legend.transitional_er: #CFE0B8 (soft sage green patch at the smooth-ER edge, marking the export zone)
colour_legend.transport_vesicles: #7FC8A9 (mint green), matching the COPII-vesicle convention already used on the Golgi-apparatus plate
colour_legend.outer_nuclear_membrane_continuity: #6E7B8B (muted slate blue), matching the nuclear-envelope tone used on the nucleus plate, flowing directly into the rough-ER grey-blue
colour_legend.golgi_context: desaturated echo of the Golgi plate's amber-to-indigo gradient at ~40% opacity, small and off to one side, if shown at all
colour_legend.note: The ER has no colour in life and TEM is greyscale; every colour here is teaching convention. The palette's job is to make the rough-to-smooth transition legible at a glance (related but distinct grey-blues, ribosome dots present vs. absent) while echoing the tones already established for the Golgi apparatus and nucleus plates in this same organelle set.

sources.title: Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell - 'The Endoplasmic Reticulum' (NCBI Bookshelf NBK26841)
sources.note: Canonical description of the ER as a netlike labyrinth of branching tubules and flattened sacs, all interconnected so the ER membrane forms one continuous sheet enclosing a single internal lumen occupying >10% of total cell volume; ER membrane >50% of total cell membrane. Rough ER = ribosome-studded cisternae doing co-translational protein import/folding/quality control; smooth ER = ribosome-free tubules, prominent in steroid-secreting cells and hepatocytes (lipoprotein synthesis, cytochrome P450 drug detoxification), and as the calcium-storing sarcoplasmic reticulum in muscle. Transitional ER = ER exit sites where COPII transport vesicles bud for the Golgi.

sources.title: StatPearls - 'Histology, Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum' (NCBI Bookshelf NBK563126)
sources.note: Confirms rough ER's defining feature is membrane-bound ribosomes on the cytosolic face via the Sec61 translocon, co-translational translocation into the lumen, and continuity with the outer nuclear membrane at the nuclear envelope.

sources.title: Dr. Jastrow's Electron Microscopic Atlas - Rough ER (EMRER) and Smooth ER (EMSER/EMSERE)
sources.note: TEM-based structural description used to cross-check morphology: rough ER as a 3D cavity system of cisternae/tubules/vesicles with ribosomes at fairly regular intervals on the outer surface; smooth ER as a branching tubular network, membrane pair spaced ~20-50 nm apart, no ribosomes. Also source for the Terminologia Histologica Latin terms 'reticulum endoplasmicum granulosum' (rough) and 'reticulum endoplasmicum nongranulosum' (smooth).

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e / Anatomy & Physiology - Endoplasmic Reticulum
sources.note: Teaching-level confirmation of rough-ER/smooth-ER terminology, the rough-to-smooth transition, and smooth ER's roles in lipid synthesis, detoxification and calcium storage; general audience-check source.

sources.title: Wikipedia (en) - Endoplasmic reticulum
sources.note: Cross-check for tubule/cisterna dimensions, ribosome particle size (~25-30 nm), and the sarcoplasmic reticulum as specialised smooth ER in muscle.

sources.title: Wikipedia (de) - Endoplasmatisches Retikulum
sources.note: German terminology check: endoplasmatisches Retikulum, raues/glattes ER, Zisternen, Ribosomen, Übergangs-ER (transitorisches ER), sarkoplasmatisches Retikulum.

sources.title: Terminologia Histologica (FIPAT/IFAA)
sources.note: Basis for the Latin terms used: reticulum endoplasmicum, reticulum endoplasmicum granulosum/nongranulosum, cisterna, lumen, ribosoma.

reference_micrograph_candidates.title: Clara cell lung - TEM.jpg
reference_micrograph_candidates.attribution: Louisa Howard, Rippel Electron Microscope Facility, Dartmouth College (via Wikimedia Commons)
reference_micrograph_candidates.note: CHOSEN. A bronchiolar exocrine (club/Clara) cell whose cytoplasm is dominated by an exceptionally clear, extensive whorled stack of rough-ER cisternae filling most of the frame, plus several mitochondria and part of a nucleus (with a visible nucleolus and chromatin) at lower right. 640x480 native, public domain, same trusted Dartmouth REMF source already used for this set's nucleus, mitochondrion and Golgi-apparatus plates. Trade-off, stated honestly: this plate shows ROUGH ER only - no smooth-ER tubule region is distinguishable in frame, and individual ribosome studding is only faintly resolvable at this compression/magnification (the sheets read as finely corrugated rather than crisply dotted). No plate in the available freely-licensed set clearly captured both regions in one frame, which the research also flagged as rare in practice; the labelled/illustrated styles carry the rough-to-smooth contrast explicitly since the real micrograph cannot.
